svg.text: A chain running from definitions through the crisis's origins and evidence to its causes, then its responses and
reforms — each stage building on the one above it, with two crowded stages (causes, and responses/reform) expanded

g.text: A chain: define the problem, trace its outbreak, survey the evidence, diagnose two kinds of cause, then follow the
reactions — public, academic, and institutional — that try to fix it.

g.title: Replication crisis: findings that won't reproduce — → spya-kv0w8d
Vocabulary: p-values, power, effect size — → spya-cxcn8h
Early-2010s failures (priming, ESP, cancer) spark the crisis — → spya-yru28f
Across fields, roughly half of findings fail to replicate — → spya-bha57y

g.text: Two parallel columns, not a sequence: failures in how science is published sit beside failures in how studies are
designed and analyzed, each sufficient on its own to make findings unreplicable.

g.text: Public reaction, then reform, then broader change
A short chain (public reaction, academic clash, credibility revolution) opens into two grouped sets of parallel
efforts: concrete publishing reforms, and broader changes to how science itself is practiced.

g.title: Public mostly unaware, sees replication as quality control — → spya-qht6nk
